terms: Region where gravity is so strong even light cannot escape.

Imaginary sphere around Earth with stars fixed on it.
Star that never sets, always above horizon.

An imaginary sphere surrounding the Earth onto which all stars appear projected, used to describe and locate objects in the night sky.
A recognised pattern of stars in a region of the sky used by observers to navigate; the IAU defines 88 official constellations.
The gradual increase in the eye's sensitivity in darkness, taking about 20 to 30 minutes, which lets an observer see fainter stars.
Excess artificial light that brightens the night sky and hides faint stars, a key reason observatories are built in remote, dark sites.
